pub mod accumulate {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_accumulate__go_func__mix
    /// Folds the values together with the operators a hash uses.
    ///
    /// `^=`, `|=` and `*=` are the three most common compound forms in the surveyed source after `+=`,
    /// and all four are the same translation.
    pub fn mix(values: Vec<i64>) -> i64 {
        let mut acc = (1) as i64;
        for i in 0..values.len() as i64 {
            acc ^= values[(i) as usize];
            acc = acc.wrapping_mul(3);
            acc |= 1;
        }
        acc
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_accumulate__go_func__shift
    /// Scales n by a power of two, in place.
    pub fn shift(mut n: i64, by: i64) -> i64 {
        n <<= by;
        n = n.wrapping_sub(1);
        n
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_accumulate__go_func__total
    /// Sums the values, accumulating in place.
    pub fn total(values: Vec<i64>) -> i64 {
        let mut sum = (0) as i64;
        for i in 0..values.len() as i64 {
            sum = sum.wrapping_add(values[(i) as usize]);
        }
        sum
    }
}

pub mod fallible {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_fallible__go_func__check
    /// Reports whether s is usable, returning only a failure.
    ///
    /// The no-value shape: `error` alone. The target has to invent the success value here, because a
    /// function that returns only a failure still has to say it succeeded.
    pub fn check(s: String) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        if s == "" {
            return Err(Box::<dyn std::error::Error>::from("empty"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_fallible__go_func__length
    /// Reports the length of s, failing on the empty string.
    ///
    /// The one-value-and-a-failure shape: `(int, error)`, which is what most of a real package looks
    /// like.
    pub fn length(s: String) -> Result<i64, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        if s == "" {
            return Err(Box::<dyn std::error::Error>::from("empty"));
        }
        Ok(s.len() as i64)
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_fallible__go_func__twice
    /// Returns the length of s doubled.
    ///
    /// The PROPAGATION shape, and the point of the whole exercise: `n, err := Length(s)` followed by
    /// `if err != nil { return 0, err }` is two statements the caller could simply not have written.
    /// The target spells it as one operator on a value that cannot be used without addressing the
    /// failure.
    pub fn twice(s: String) -> Result<i64, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        let n = length(s)?;
        Ok(n.wrapping_add(n))
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_fallible__go_func__validate
    /// Checks s and reports nothing else.
    ///
    /// Propagation with NO value bound: the call is run for its failure alone, so there is nothing to
    /// name and the target keeps it as a statement.
    pub fn validate(s: String) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        check(s)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub mod handoff {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_handoff__go_func__bump
    /// Adds one through the pointer, so the parameter is an exclusive borrow and the argument
    /// lends exclusively.
    pub fn bump(c: &mut Counter) {
        c.total = c.total.wrapping_add(1);
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_handoff__go_func__read
    /// Returns the count without writing, so the parameter is a shared borrow.
    pub fn read(c: &Counter) -> i64 {
        c.total
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_handoff__go_func__twice
    /// Bumps the counter twice, handing the same local to a borrowing parameter each time.
    pub fn twice() -> i64 {
        let mut c = Counter { total: 0 };
        bump(&mut c);
        bump(&mut c);
        read(&c)
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_handoff__go_struct_body__counter

pub mod invariant {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_invariant__go_func__half
    /// Returns n halved, and aborts on an odd input.
    ///
    /// The invariant shape: a condition the caller is required to have met, and a literal message
    /// naming what it was.
    pub fn half(n: i64) -> i64 {
        if n.wrapping_rem(2) != 0 {
            panic!("Half requires an even argument");
        }
        n.wrapping_div(2)
    }
}

pub mod pointers {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_pointers__go_struct_body__counter
    /// Accumulates a total.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
    pub struct Counter {
        /// The running sum.
        total: i64,
        /// Names the counter.
        label: String,
    }
    impl Counter {
        /// Adds n to the counter.
        ///
        /// MUTATED, does not escape: the body assigns through the receiver and nothing outlives the call.
        pub fn add(&mut self, n: i64) {
            self.total = self.total.wrapping_add(n);
        }
        /// Reports the counter's name, by value receiver.
        ///
        /// No pointer at all — the receiver is a copy, so no disposition question arises.
        pub fn label(&self) -> String {
            self.label.clone()
        }
        /// Folds other into the receiver.
        ///
        /// The receiver is mutated; `other` is read-only. Two pointers in one signature, with different
        /// answers — a rule that keys on the type rather than on the facts gives them the same one.
        pub fn merge(&mut self, other: &Counter) {
            self.total = self.total.wrapping_add(other.total);
        }
        /// Reports the accumulated value.
        ///
        /// Neither mutated nor escaping: a read-only borrow is enough.
        pub fn total(&self) -> i64 {
            self.total
        }
    }
}
pub mod scoped {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_scoped__go_func__span
    /// Reports the width of s, counting a short string as one wider than it is.
    ///
    /// The binding is read in BOTH branches, which is what makes the block the only faithful shape: a
    /// name hoisted out of the `if` would still be live after it, and this one must not be.
    pub fn span(s: String) -> i64 {
        let mut result = 0;
        {
            let size = s.len() as i64;
            if size > 4 {
                result = size;
            } else {
                result = size.wrapping_add(1);
            };
        };
        result
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_scoped__go_func__width
    /// Reports the width of s once it clears the minimum, and zero otherwise.
    ///
    /// The plain shape: bound in the init clause, read in the condition and the branch.
    pub fn width(s: String) -> i64 {
        {
            let size = s.len() as i64;
            if size > 4 {
                return size;
            }
        };
        0
    }
}
pub mod shapes {
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_shapes__go_interface__named
    /// Anything that can render its own name.
    pub trait Named {
        /// Returns the display name.
        fn name(&self) -> String;
        /// Replaces the display name.
        fn rename(&mut self, next: String);
    }
    // region: oyatie_example_portengine_fixture_corpus_shapes__go_struct_body__point
    /// A location in two dimensions.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
    pub struct Point {
        /// The horizontal coordinate.
        pub x: i64,
        /// The vertical coordinate.
        pub y: i64,
        /// Unexported and must survive extraction as such.
        label: String,
    }
    impl Point {
        /// Reports the rectangle area between the origin and p.
        pub fn area(&self) -> i64 {
            self.x.wrapping_mul(self.y)
        }
        /// Returns a Point moved by the given deltas.
        pub fn shift(&self, dx: i64, dy: i64) -> Point {
            Point {
                x: self.x.wrapping_add(dx),
                y: self.y.wrapping_add(dy),
                label: String::new(),
            }
        }
    }
